articles.title: Valmir de Francisquinho: propostas para saúde e empresas em 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato visitou moradores no bairro Veneza, na capital, se reuniu com a equipe de campanha e fez carreata em Nossa Senhora do Socorro.
articles.summary: Valmir de Francisquinho visitou o bairro Veneza e defendeu a descentralização da saúde e o apoio ao empresariado sergipano durante agenda das Eleições 2026.
articles.body:
Nesta segunda-feira (28), o jornalismo do g1 e da TV Sergipe deu continuidade ao acompanhamento das agendas dos candidatos ao governo de Sergipe. A ordem de veiculação das reportagens foi definida em reunião com representantes de todos os partidos e coligações.

O candidato Valmir de Francisquinho (Republicanos) visitou o bairro Veneza, na capital, onde conversou com moradores e comerciantes da região, se reuniu com a equipe de campanha e finalizou o dia em uma carreata em Nossa Senhora do Socorro. Ele falou à equipe da TV Sergipe sobre as prioridades do governo nos próximos quatro anos caso seja eleito.

Valmir de Francisquinho disputa o governo de Sergipe pelo Republicanos — Foto: TV Sergipe

“Construir um novo hospital na Grande Aracaju, fazer a descentralização da saúde, pegar o Banco do Estado para voltar a ser um banco de fomento para ajudar o empresariado sergipano e cuidar da falta d'água e dessas contas exorbitantes no estado de Sergipe”, disse.

articles.title: Casa em Orlando ganha espaço como estratégia para proteger patrimônio | G1
articles.standfirst: Brasileiros buscam imóveis na Flórida, nos EUA, como estratégia de diversificação, proteção e redução de riscos.
articles.summary: Brasileiros buscam imóveis na Flórida, nos EUA, como estratégia de diversificação, proteção e redução de riscos.
articles.body:
Residência em Orlando é estratégia para proteger patrimônio do brasileiro — Foto: Divulgação

Blindagem patrimonial, preservação, diversificação, segurança e planejamento são conceitos que aparecem com frequência quando o assunto é proteger o patrimônio construído ao longo dos anos. Para famílias que concentram imóveis, empresas e investimentos financeiros no Brasil, manter uma parcela dos ativos em outra economia e em outra moeda pode reduzir a concentração e o risco cambial do patrimônio.

Isso porque o cenário de 2026 adicionou um elemento novo a essa discussão: depois de anos marcados por forte valorização e baixa oferta, o mercado americano entrou em um período de maior estoque, maior seletividade e, em determinados segmentos e regiões, maior capacidade de negociação por parte do comprador.

O mercado imobiliário nos EUA chama a atenção de investidores de diferentes nacionalidades. A Flórida permanece como o principal destino de compradores estrangeiros de imóveis nos Estados Unidos, segundo levantamento da National Association of Realtors (NAR). No período de abril de 2024 a março de 2025, o estado concentrou 21% de todas as compras realizadas por estrangeiros no mercado americano.

Mas comprar casa em Orlando para proteger patrimônio? Como funciona isso na prática?

O Brasil aparece entre os países que mais movimentam o mercado imobiliário internacional da Flórida. Segundo a Florida Realtors, os brasileiros representaram 7% dos compradores internacionais no período analisado, atrás de Canadá, com 18%, e Colômbia, com 10%.

Orlando também ocupa posição de destaque. A região metropolitana de Orlando-Kissimmee-Sanford concentrou 13% das compras realizadas por estrangeiros na Flórida, ficando atrás apenas da região de Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach, com 45%.

Leonardo Martins é CEO, broker e cofundador do The Florida Lounge — Foto: Divulgação

Uma família que concentra imóveis, investimentos financeiros e outros bens exclusivamente no Brasil está exposta às condições econômicas, cambiais e regulatórias de um único país.

Comprar um imóvel nos Estados Unidos pode representar, dentro de uma estratégia mais ampla, uma forma de diversificação patrimonial, já que o ativo está localizado em outro mercado e tem seu valor denominado em dólares.

Isso não significa, porém, que um imóvel seja uma proteção automática contra crises ou perdas. O mercado imobiliário também sofre oscilações. Existem custos de aquisição, impostos, seguros, manutenção, condomínio, administração e eventuais despesas de venda.

"Quando falamos em proteção patrimonial, não estamos falando que um imóvel é imune às oscilações do mercado. Estamos falando em diversificação. O patrimônio passa a estar em outro país, em outra moeda e dentro de outro ambiente econômico. O diferencial aqui está em investir com a empresa que informa sobre o que é real neste mercado, porque tem experiência e credibilidade para tomar as melhores decisões" , explica Leonardo Martins, CEO, broker e cofundador do The Florida Lounge .

A empresa atua no mercado imobiliário da Flórida e trabalha com brasileiros interessados em morar, investir ou construir patrimônio nos Estados Unidos.

Para Leonardo, a principal dificuldade enfrentada pelo comprador brasileiro nem sempre é encontrar um imóvel. "Hoje existe muita informação disponível. O problema é separar informação de ruído. O nosso trabalho começa antes de apresentar uma casa. É entender o momento da família, o objetivo daquele patrimônio e responder às perguntas que precisam ser respondidas antes da decisão", acrescenta.

A decisão de comprar um imóvel em outro país envolve aspectos que vão além da escolha da casa. "Essa decisão exige muito mais do que olhar para o preço da casa ou para uma eventual valorização. É fundamental entender como funciona o mercado americano, quais são os custos, as regras, a tributação, o modelo de locação e, principalmente, as diferenças culturais e jurídicas em relação ao Brasil" , explica o economista Carlos Albane.

A análise também deve considerar o objetivo do comprador, o horizonte de investimento, a disponibilidade financeira e a capacidade de arcar com custos recorrentes. Em outras palavras, diversificar não significa simplesmente comprar um imóvel no exterior. É necessário entender qual papel aquele ativo terá dentro do patrimônio como um todo.

“O mercado americano deixou de ser apenas um mercado de valorização e voltou a ser um mercado de seleção. Alguns anos atrás, em determinadas regiões, o desafio era conseguir comprar. Hoje existe mais estoque e mais possibilidade de negociação. Isso aumenta a importância de escolher corretamente o ativo” , afirma Glauco Pochine, CEO Internacional e cofundador do The Florida Lounge.

Comprar para morar, investir ou ter uma segunda residência?

Um dos pontos que mais diferencia as compras internacionais é a finalidade do imóvel. Uma propriedade adquirida para moradia tem características diferentes daquela destinada à locação. Uma casa utilizada para férias também pode exigir uma análise específica sobre localização, regras do condomínio, administração e custos.

A pesquisa da Florida Realtors mostra justamente essa diversidade de objetivos: 68% dos compradores internacionais na Flórida planejavam utilizar o imóvel para aluguel residencial, como casa de férias ou para uma combinação entre aluguel e férias.

Entre os brasileiros, 15% indicaram a intenção de utilizar o imóvel como residência principal. Outros 23% apontaram aluguel residencial, 26% férias e 25% uma combinação entre férias e aluguel.

Para Pochine, entender essa finalidade é uma das etapas mais importantes. "Não existe um imóvel perfeito para todo mundo. Existe o imóvel que faz sentido para determinado objetivo. Por isso, antes de falar de metragem, piscina ou número de quartos, precisamos entender por que aquela pessoa quer comprar nos Estados Unidos" , afirma.

Quanto custa e como os estrangeiros compram?

Glauco Pochine é CEO Internacional e cofundador do The Florida Lounge — Foto: Divulgação

O levantamento da Florida Realtors mostra que o preço mediano pago por compradores internacionais na Flórida foi de US$ 442 mil no período analisado, enquanto a mediana de todos os imóveis residenciais vendidos no estado ficou em US$ 390 mil.

Outro dado chama atenção: 60% dos compradores internacionais na Flórida pagaram suas aquisições à vista. No mercado americano como um todo, o percentual de compradores internacionais que pagaram em dinheiro foi de 47%.

Isso não significa, porém, que a compra internacional esteja restrita a investidores que possuem todo o valor disponível. Há diferentes modelos de aquisição e financiamento, que precisam ser avaliados de acordo com o perfil do comprador e as regras aplicáveis.

A atratividade de Orlando não está limitada ao turismo. A região metropolitana reúne uma economia diversificada, crescimento populacional, infraestrutura, universidades, saúde, logística e uma ampla oferta imobiliária que atende desde residências principais até imóveis destinados à locação tradicional e ao mercado de férias.

Para o investidor, entretanto, essa diversidade também exige atenção. Orlando não deve ser analisada como um único mercado. A dinâmica de Winter Garden, Lake Nona, Clermont, Kissimmee ou de condomínios voltados para short-term rental pode ser bastante diferente.

No primeiro trimestre de 2026, Orlando apareceu como o quarto mercado imobiliário americano mais acessado por compradores internacionais no Realtor.com, atrás de Miami, Los Angeles e Nova York, segundo a Florida Realtors.

A loja do The Florida Lounge no Vogue Square, na Barra da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Divulgação

Comprar uma casa nos Estados Unidos não cria, por si só, uma blindagem patrimonial. A expressão pode ser utilizada para descrever uma estratégia mais ampla de organização e diversificação de ativos, mas não significa que o patrimônio estará protegido de qualquer risco.

Um imóvel pode sofrer desvalorização, ficar desocupado, gerar despesas inesperadas ou enfrentar mudanças nas regras tributárias e imobiliárias. Por isso, a compra precisa ser analisada em conjunto com outros aspectos da vida financeira do investidor.

Uma família com investimentos concentrados exclusivamente no Brasil está sujeita ao ambiente econômico, regulatório e cambial brasileiro, já que a dolarização patrimonial por meio de um imóvel não deve ser confundida simplesmente com uma aposta na valorização do dólar, mas como um ativo real localizado em outra economia, sujeito a uma dinâmica própria de preços e que, dependendo da estratégia adotada, pode também gerar renda em moeda americana.

É nesse ambiente de excesso de informação que empresas especializadas em atender brasileiros no mercado americano tentam se posicionar. "Para o The Florida Lounge, é motivo de orgulho atuar há nove anos com presença permanente no Brasil, mantendo operações em São Paulo e no Rio de Janeiro. Somos a única imobiliária americana com presença permanente no Brasil. Essa proximidade nos permite acompanhar o investidor antes, durante e depois da aquisição nos Estados Unidos" , detalha Glauco.

A proposta, segundo a empresa, é funcionar como uma ponte entre o comprador brasileiro e o mercado imobiliário americano. "Somos uma empresa de vendas, evidentemente. Mas acreditamos que a venda deve ser consequência de um trabalho bem feito. Quando conseguimos explicar o cenário, os números, os custos, os riscos e as oportunidades, o cliente consegue tomar uma decisão consciente" , afirma Martins.

O processo, segundo a empresa, não termina na escolha da propriedade. Documentação, financiamento, impostos, seguros, administração e eventual locação também precisam entrar na conta.

O que analisar antes de comprar o imóvel?

Para quem considera utilizar um imóvel americano dentro de uma estratégia patrimonial, alguns pontos merecem atenção:

● Objetivo da compra - É para morar, passar férias, alugar ou diversificar patrimônio?;

●Localização - A região precisa fazer sentido para o objetivo definido;

● Custo total - Além do preço da casa, entram impostos, seguro, condomínio, manutenção e administração;

● Tributação - A compra e eventual renda de aluguel podem envolver obrigações fiscais nos Estados Unidos e no Brasil;

●L iquidez - Nem todo imóvel é vendido com a mesma facilidade. Localização e características da propriedade influenciam esse aspecto;

●E xposição cambial - Um ativo em dólar diversifica o patrimônio, mas também está sujeito à variação do câmbio;

●E strutura patrimonial - Dependendo do patrimônio e do objetivo, questões sucessórias, tributárias e societárias podem exigir orientação especializada.

O dólar é importante, mas não é a única variável. “Para brasileiros, o câmbio inevitavelmente entra na análise. Uma alta do dólar encarece a aquisição para quem está transferindo recursos em reais. Por outro lado, avaliar um investimento internacional exclusivamente pela cotação da moeda pode deixar de fora outras variáveis importantes, como preço do imóvel neste momento, capacidade de negociação, renda potencial e horizonte de permanência do investimento” , detalha Glauco.

O mercado americano segue interessante, mas ficou mais complexo atualmente. É fundamental encontrar o especialista certo que vai guiar toda a jornada do investidor. "Nosso papel é colocar todas essas informações na mesa. Análise, informação precisa, planejamento confiável. Às vezes, a melhor decisão é comprar. Em outras situações, é esperar. O mais importante é que a pessoa saiba por que está fazendo aquilo" , afirma o CEO.

Para quem avalia investir em imóveis nos Estados Unidos, buscar informação com quem conhece profundamente esse mercado pode ser uma etapa decisiva antes da compra. O papel de uma empresa especializada é ajudar o investidor a compreender cenários, custos, oportunidades, riscos e as diferenças entre os mercados brasileiro e americano. Nesse modelo, a venda deixa de ser o ponto de partida e passa a ser consequência de um processo baseado em informação, confiança e autoridade sobre o mercado.

O The Florida Lounge possui lounges nos Estados Unidos, no Brasil (Rio de Janeiro e São Paulo) e um time especializado em Portugal.

articles.title: UE conclui que produções de frango e mel do Brasil atendem requisitos para exportações | G1
articles.standfirst: O relatório ainda não significa que o Brasil poderá voltar a exportar os dois produtos ao bloco, mas representa mais um passo no processo de reinclusão na lista de fornecedores dos países membros.
articles.summary: O relatório ainda não significa que o Brasil poderá voltar a exportar os dois produtos ao bloco, mas representa mais um passo no processo de reinclusão na lista de fornecedores dos países membros.
articles.body:
A Comissão Europeia publicou um relatório oficial, nesta segunda-feira (28), em que considera satisfatória a qualidade do sistema brasileiro de produção das cadeias de carne de aves e mel.

Segundo o Ministério da Agricultura do Brasil, o documento concluiu que "o arcabouço legal, os procedimentos, a capacitação dos fiscais e os controles oficiais brasileiros são capazes de fornecer as garantias exigidas pela legislação europeia".

O relatório, no entanto, ainda não significa que o Brasil poderá voltar a exportar os dois produtos ao bloco, mas representa mais um passo no processo de reinclusão na lista de fornecedores dos países membros.

O Ministério da Agricultura solicitou a inclusão do relatório na pauta da reunião técnica do Comitê Permanente de Plantas, Animais, Alimentos e Rações (Scopaff) da Comissão Europeia, responsável pela decisão final, que vai acontecer nos dias 20 e 21 de outubro de 2026.

🔍 A UE tirou o Brasil da lista de países que cumprem as suas regras sobre o uso de antimicrobianos na pecuária . Essas substâncias são usadas para tratar infecções em animais, mas o bloco proíbe seu uso para estimular o crescimento. Também proíbe o uso, em animais, de antimicrobianos reservados ao tratamento de seres humanos. ( Embargo ao Brasil )

A missão europeia realizou visitas a estabelecimentos produtivos brasileiros de carne de aves e produtos avícolas, mel e produtos apícolas, e órgãos oficiais entre os dias 24 de agosto e 4 de setembro.

Nas visitas, foi verificado a proibição do uso de antimicrobianos como promotores de crescimento e aumento de rendimento.

O Ministério da Agricultura informou que aguarda o cumprimento por parte da União Europeia das etapas administrativas necessárias para a conclusão do processo.

No dia 3 de setembro, começou a valer o embargo da União Europeia a produtos de origem animal do Brasil. Com a medida, o país fica impedido de exportar carne bovina, suína, frango, mel, pescados e ovos para as 27 nações do bloco.

A decisão pode ser revertida, a depender das negociações entre a UE e o governo brasileiro.

O anúncio da exclusão do Brasil da lista de fornecedores foi feita em maio.

A medida não foi motivada por irregularidades encontradas na carne brasileira, mas pela avaliação da União Europeia de que o controle feito pelo Brasil sobre o uso dessas substâncias é insuficiente.

As carnes bovina e de frango são os produtos mais afetados, pois estão entre os itens de origem animal mais exportados pelo Brasil para a UE. Ainda assim, representam uma parcela pequena do valor total exportado pelo país.

articles.title: Bond Veteran Jim Bianco Turns Bullish for First Time Since 2020
articles.summary: Jim Bianco, a Wall Street veteran and longtime market watcher, is turning bullish on US Treasuries for the first time in six years after benchmark yields sur...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Jim Bianco, a Wall Street veteran and longtime market watcher, is turning bullish on US Treasuries for the first time in six years after benchmark yields surged to two-decade highs, creating an enticing entry point.

"This is a value play," said Bianco, president and founder of Chicago-based Bianco Research. "If we start to see yields going higher, I'm going to continue to get in."

Sentiment toward bonds has sharply deteriorated in recent weeks, hurt by a confluence of factors including surging energy prices, persistent fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, a resilient US economy and heavy technology investment to fund the artificial-intelligence boom. On Monday, the 10-year yield surged to 5.27%, the highest since 2007, as rising oil prices prompted traders to boost bets that the Federal Reserve will keep raising interest rates.

While the selloff may have further to run, Bianco said that yields above 5% across most maturities make the risk-reward of owning bonds increasingly attractive. As a result, he increased interest-rate exposure – or duration — in an actively managed index he oversees that underpins a WisdomTree exchange-traded fund. The index's duration has risen to more than 6 years, compared with 5.7 years for the Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index.

"Everybody's ridiculously bearish on the bond market right now," Bianco said. "I'm getting a big fat cushion for buying bonds at 5.2%. Now's not the time to be losing your mind over it."

Bianco, whose 40-year plus career includes stints at First Boston and UBS before founding Bianco Research in 1998, said he had been bearish on the bond market since 2020, when 10-year Treasury yields touched an all-time low of 0.3% during the depth of pandemic. Now, with yields on the rise, the bond math is becoming more favorable.

Investors who buy 10-year Treasuries at current levels would need to see yields rise to around 6% over the next year before price losses wipe out the bond's income, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The return profile is also asymmetric: A percentage-point increase in yields would produce a loss of less than 2%, while a decline of the same magnitude would generate a return of about 13%.

images.caption: Jim Bianco is turning bullish on Treasuries as rising yields make getting in now more and more attractive. · Bloomberg · Photographer: Hollie Adams/Bloomberg

articles.title: The reason your healthcare premiums are skyrocketing? AI.
articles.summary: The Blue Cross Blue Shield Association released a new report showing that hospitals' use of AI is the biggest factor behind increased healthcare spending.
articles.body:
Rising healthcare costs are hammering Americans, and now artificial intelligence is raising the price tag even more.

The Blue Cross Blue Shield Association (BCBSA), a consortium of insurers, released a new report showing that hospitals' use of AI is the biggest factor behind nearly $1 billion in added healthcare spending for the Blue Cross Blue Shield companies over two years.

The upshot of those additional payments made to hospitals: higher insurance premiums for you and me.

And the insurers contend that patients did not receive any extra treatments for the extra billings.

"Our research showed that there was a change in the way patients were coded, but no evidence of a corresponding change in the care delivered," David Merritt, senior vice president of external affairs at the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association, told Yahoo Finance.

The analysis of claims data between 2023 and 2025 found that "as more hospitals apply AI coding tools, an increasing number of patients are coded as medically complex."

Blue Cross Blue ​Shield Association's network of independent health insurance companies covers 1 in 3 Americans.

Using AI tools, hospitals are vacuuming up more information about their patients and submitting fatter claims, according to the BCBSA findings.

What that means is that patients often fall into a higher-cost billing category after a secondary diagnosis, flagged by AI, in addition to the condition that brought them in originally.

The secondary diagnoses for conditions like low sodium or anemia move the claim into a higher-paying category, according to the analysis.

AI-assisted billing software scans records and lab data for anything that can be coded, according to the research. With a majority of hospitals now tapping AI coding tools to document patient appointments and dissect lab tests and physicians' notes, insurers are responding by upping premiums.

"When the same care costs more, it flows through the system, driving up premiums and out-of-pocket costs for families who are already struggling with higher prices," Merritt said.

Soaring healthcare premiums are a serious concern for Americans.

The median proposed premium increase for 2027 is 15%, according to an analysis from the healthcare research nonprofit KFF. That's likely to be the second consecutive year of double-digit premium hikes. This year, the median rate increase was 20%.

articles.title: Former Microsoft strategy chief explains why most digital ads 'are not very good' — and how AI will help
articles.summary: Internet ads are ineffective, Stagwell CEO Mark Penn is quick to point out, and AI could make a chance to make them better.
articles.body:
Most internet ads are ineffective, Stagwell ( STGW ) CEO Mark Penn is quick to point out, and AI could make them better.

"Most digital ads are not very good," Penn, formerly chief strategy officer at Microsoft ( MSFT ), told Power Players with Brian Sozzi (video above). "You run through hundreds and hundreds of those in a day, and they have virtually no impact on you, by and large."

Stagwell provides creative, technology, media, and research services to major brands and organizations. Penn, who said he was "really co-CMO" at Microsoft at one point, explained that the potential payoff from AI isn't doing the old work more cheaply.

"People always make the mistake of thinking that new technology is about simplifying the stuff we used to do," he said. "New technology is about doing things we always wished we could do, but couldn't do in the past."

AI is "revolutionizing production," Penn said, and the bar for advertisers goes up with it.

"There's more of a premium now on getting the right ad to the right person at the right time with something that is ... really interesting and engaging," he said.

Asked whether AI would crush the ad industry, Penn said, "AI is more, much more of our friend, actually."

He explained that Stagwell has created "a series of products we call the machine," and demand is up: "We have more people looking for premium creative ... and more people looking for digital transformation than ever."

Internal AI tools helped us analyze transcripts. Humans wrote and edited this post.

articles.title: Sensex slips 1.1K points to 6-month low: D-Street sees red as Gulf crisis, poor monsoon cloud outlook
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Thanks partially to Monday's sell-off on Dalal Street, the stock price of recently listed NSE slid below its IPO price for the first time and
articles.body: MUMBAI: Thanks partially to Monday's sell-off on Dalal Street, the stock price of recently listed NSE slid below its IPO price for the first time and closed at that level. With foreign funds leading the day's sell-off, sensex lost 1,124 points (1.5%) to close at 72,771 points, nearly a six-month low level. And on NSE, Nifty lost 360 points (1.6%) to close at 22,780 points, also its lowest close since March 30 this year.A host of factors led to the day's slide in the market. The rupee neared the 96-per-dollar mark again, while Brent crude spiked to near the $100/barrel level, after signs of escalation of the war in the Persian Gulf region emerged. On the domestic front, the impact of a weak monsoon pushing up inflation, interest rates and bond yields also weighed on investor sentiment, market players said.In Monday's market, on BSE the stock price of NSE opened just a tad above its IPO price of Rs 1,785, dipped to an intraday low of Rs 1,761 and closed at Rs 1,763, down 1.7% on the day. On the day of listing, Sept 24, the stock had touched an intraday high of Rs 1,878 and has been on a gradual slide since.In the broader market, the two benchmark indices were weighed down by weak global cues, elevated crude oil prices and bond yields, persistent foreign fund selling and heightened geopolitical uncertainty following the stalemate in the US-Iran peace talks, said Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice president-research, Bajaj Broking.The slide in the market came mainly on the back of a Rs 5,353-crore net selling by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in stocks alone. Although domestic funds, with a net buying figure of Rs 5,189 crore, nearly matched the selling by foreign players, it was not enough to fully cushion the pressure.As a result, investors' wealth lost during the day was at about Rs 7.5 lakh crore, with the market capitalisation of companies listed on BSE now at Rs 474.4 lakh crore, exchange data showed.In the international market, Brent rallied 2.2% on Monday while on Friday, the Indian crude basket was priced at nearly $121 a barrel. In comparison, in April, at the height of the war in West Asia, it had hit a high of $114.5.Rising crude prices are now threatening the domestic inflation rate, pushing up yields on Indian govt bonds and also having an adverse effect on the rupee.You use AI every day. articles.title: To avert listing, Noel submits Tata Sons revamp plan to RBI
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Weeks after Reserve Bank of India directed Tata Sons to comply with upper-layer NBFC-CIC norms, Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has proposed
articles.body: MUMBAI: Weeks after Reserve Bank of India directed Tata Sons to comply with upper-layer NBFC-CIC norms, Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has proposed merging two subsidiaries, Tata Electronics Systems (TES) and Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE), with the 109-year-old holding company to take it outside the RBI's regulatory ambit and avoid a public listing.The proposal comes barely 11 days after the Tata Sons board expressed its preference for a listing to comply with RBI's upper-layer regulations for a core investment company (CIC) or non-banking financial company (NBFC). At the board meeting, Noel representing the majority shareholders had opposed a listing, arguing that alternative options should be explored.Noel's present plan marks a departure from past restructuring moves, such as the demerger of TCS in 2004 into a separate entity. It would also shut the door on minority shareholder Shapoorji Pallonji Group's hopes of monetising its Tata Sons stake through an IPO. Noel has submitted the proposal to Tata Sons and RBI; their stance on the plan was not immediately clear.F N Subedar, adviser to Tata Trusts and former Tata Sons company secretary, described the plan as a return to Tata Sons' historic structure.Tata Sons had housed operating businesses such as TCS alongside being the group's holding company in the past, Subedar said. Tata Sons assumed NBFC-CIC status only after TCS was demerged.Binoy Parikh, partner at Katalyst Advisors, said the proposal may not permanently resolve Tata Sons' regulatory status. If Tata Sons were to later list Tata Electronics Systems or Tata Consulting Engineers, or induct external investors into either business, it could be forced to demerge them. That could reduce operating revenues and potentially push Tata Sons back into the NBFC-CIC category, reviving the listing obligation. "The structure is essentially a toggle that can be switched on and off depending on the regulatory outcome sought at a given point," he said.The proposal marks the group's second attempt to avoid a listing. In 2024, Tata Sons sought to exit RBI's upper-layer NBFC-CIC rules after substantially reducing debt. Earlier this month, the regulator rejected the request for deregistration and directed the company to comply with its norms.RBI's principal business criteria for an NBFC require financial assets and financial income to account for more than 50% of a company's total assets and income respectively. The proposed merger would tilt Tata Sons' income mix towards operating revenue, causing it to fail one of the two tests and thus fall outside the NBFC framework, according to a restructuring expert. The transaction could also take Tata Sons outside the definition of a Core Investment Company (CIC), which requires at least 90% of net assets to comprise investments in group companies. Tata Sons' net assets are Rs 2 lakh crore. With operating assets from the merged entities coming onto its balance sheet, investments would fall below the 90% threshold, the expert said.According to Tata Trusts, the merged entity would have had an operating revenue of Rs 1.05 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026, far in excess of its income of Rs 40,072 crore from financial assets. Operating revenue would constitute 64% of the total income of the merged entity.Subedar said the latest proposal is significantly different from Tata Sons' earlier attempt to exit the RBI's regulatory framework. "Earlier, we said we would remain a CIC. Now we are saying we would be neither an NBFC nor a CIC. That is the change," he said.Noel did not require fresh approval from the Tata Trusts boards to pursue the proposal, Subedar said. He was acting on a unanimous July 2025 resolution directing that all efforts be made to preserve Tata Sons' status as an unlisted private company.People familiar with the matter, however, disputed that interpretation. They said the July 2025 resolution cannot be automatically carried forward because the trustees' positions have since diverged, with the Trusts' two vice-chairmen backing a public listing of Tata Sons. They also said that when the resolution was passed, RBI had not yet ruled on Tata Sons' March 2024 application seeking an exit from the NBFC-CIC framework, materially altering the circumstances under which the mandate was given.The scheme would require RBI's no-objection certificate before it is placed before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for approval. It would also need shareholder approval, including the backing of at least 75% of votes cast.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Safety, profitability top priorities: Air India CEO designate
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"Safety, reliability, profitability and pursuing disciplined and sustainable growth.\" Air India's CEO and MD (proposed) Tewolde Gebremariam on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "Safety, reliability, profitability and pursuing disciplined and sustainable growth." Air India's CEO and MD (proposed) Tewolde Gebremariam on Monday set these priorities out for the struggling airline group in his first Town Hall with employees. Apart from widening losses, AI's safety practices and alleged lack of discipline among crew are under the scanner since last June's Ahmedabad crash and then the recent case of a badly rattled Phuket-Delhi flight whose pilot-in-command was subsequently sacked for failing dope test on arrival.External environment is also tough - airspace closures (particularly Pakistan), rising crude prices, rupee's weakness and global uncertainty - which are common to all Indian carriers. Foreign airlines can overfly Pakistan.Gebremariam, who is awaiting regulatory clearance to take over the role, said India's favourable demographics, strong economic growth, geographic position and large global diaspora provide a "unique foundation" for AI's future success. "These factors give us confidence that if we execute well and remain focused on our customers, AI can become not only one of the largest airlines in the world, but among the very best," the former top boss of Ethiopian Airlines, who successfully turned around that carrier, said.He also pointed out the challenging environment and thanked the over 24,000 employees for the change the airline has seen since being taken over by Tata Group in Jan 2022. "Over the past four years, a great deal has been achieved. At the same time, there remains significant opportunity ahead of us. That is what makes this an exciting moment for AI and for all of us." Addressing basic issues without getting distracted by promises of a flashy makeover, Gebremariam set the priorities for the airline which is trying to regain flyers' faith.SafetyThat "would remain the airline's foremost priority and guiding principle.... every Air Indian has a role to play... people (be) empowered to speak up, raise concerns and report issues without hesitation. If you see something, say something. The stronger our reporting culture, the stronger our safety culture," Gebremariam said.Reliability"Our customers should remember AI for its reliability. They should be confident that flights will depart and arrive on time, baggage will travel with them and when disruptions occur, we should communicate transparently and recover quickly."Improving financial performanceWhile acknowledging external factors have affected the airline's path to breakeven, he stressed AI cannot afford to lose focus on financial performance. "We must improve both revenue and cost performance... Every employee can contribute to savings, and those savings add up across an organisation of our scale."Sustainable growth"Growth is the oxygen of business. But growth must also be profitable and sustainable. We will pursue expansion in a disciplined manner and ensure our people, fleet and network are ready to support it."You use AI every day. articles.title: Oil Extends Gain as Iran Uncertainty Outweighs Saudi Pipe Return
articles.summary: Oil rose a second day as uncertainty over progress in US-Iran talks weighed against signs of strong demand and a resumption of flows through a key pipeline f...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Oil rose a second day as uncertainty over progress in US-Iran talks weighed against signs of strong demand and a resumption of flows through a key pipeline from top exporter Saudi Arabia.

West Texas Intermediate advanced above $93 a barrel after ticking higher in the previous session, while Brent closed near $105. Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before US midterm elections in November, following US President Donald Trump's rejection of a proposal to reopen the waterway in seven days.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has restored about half the flows through its cross-country East-West pipeline, a crucial route bypassing the strait, after drone strikes halted operations earlier this month. Flows through the link to the Red Sea have reached at least 3.5 million barrels a day, according to people familiar with the matter.

The fundamental outlook for oil is turning increasingly bullish, and key gauges of supply tightness have spiked in recent days in a sign of a clamor for barrels that can be delivered quickly, while fuel prices are surging as global refinery capacity remains hobbled. Crude is headed for a third monthly gain on the escalating US-Iran tensions, disruptions to the Saudi bypass route and potential diesel export curbs by Washington.

articles.title: As consumers go big on experiences, private equity follows
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Private equity (PE) money is chasing the events and experiences economy in India-think KKR's bet on ticketing and live entertainment platform
articles.body: MUMBAI: Private equity (PE) money is chasing the events and experiences economy in India-think KKR's bet on ticketing and live entertainment platform BookMyShow or Blackstone's investment in an Indian Premier League (IPL) franchise. Young consumers are now driving household spends and they are allocating a big chunk of their budgets to experiences.Consider this: at Travis Scott's Delhi concert last year, nearly 100,000 tickets were sold within minutes. That roughly translates into India spending almost Rs 100 crore within minutes on a cultural phenomenon, analysts at EY said. Investors want to latch on to this trend early and take a share of these emerging consumption spaces."Experiences over things are a mega-trend. This shift is happening across categories and segments. Consumption patterns of young people will never be the same as that of the previous generation," said Vikram Kumaraswamy, partner at L Catterton.There are some numbers to substantiate the growing scale of the space-estimates by analysts at KPMG showed that the local live events and entertainment market touched Rs 13,600 crore (as of 2025). Riding on the cricket fan base, IPL ticket sales grew to about Rs 500 crore in 2025 from around Rs 120 crore in 2008, data sourced from investment bank Houlihan Lokey showed.The broader commercial sports economy covering media rights, athlete endorsements, sponsorships and franchise revenues is pegged at Rs 18,864 crore. "In an era increasingly dominated by AI, screen fatigue, and algorithm-driven digital consumption, live sports and fitness ecosystems stand out as the ultimate non-replicable, experiential asset class, which is why institutional private equity is aggressively leaning in," said Sameer Jindal, MD at Houlihan Lokey.For PE investors, that irreplaceable real-world emotional pull translates into rare pricing power, highly resilient linear/digital media rights, diversified stadium and merchandise monetisation and an enduring consumer moat against the digital noise, Jindal added.It was a stellar 350% return made by CVC in four years by selling a majority stake in Gujarat Titans to Torrent Group that triggered fresh PE interest in IPL. "As our demography is changing and the whole social media world is creating a very different consumer response to everything... we as investors need to find the right opportunities to participate in and benefit from the underlying growth," said Narendra Ostawal, MD and head of India PE at Warburg Pincus.Businesses linked to providing experiences will do better. Even firms having a play in the product side will try and associate their brands with experiences. For instance, a brand could promote healthy snacking during a sports event, said Kumaraswamy. L Catterton will invest in businesses building around propositions such as better home experiences, travel and fitness."The returns profile for new businesses are not that straightforward. The consumer acquisition cost is high. We have to make sure we invest in businesses that have the operating leverage to grow sustainably in the long-run," Kumaraswamy said.You use AI every day. articles.title: IIP growth surges to 8% in August
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Industrial production rose 8% in Aug as against 4.7% expansion recorded a year ago, on account of robust growth in manufacturing and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Industrial production rose 8% in Aug as against 4.7% expansion recorded a year ago, on account of robust growth in manufacturing and electricity sectors.Sequentially also, industrial production witnessed acceleration from an upward revised figure of 7.4% in July, latest data released Monday showed. For the first five months of 2026-27, the index of industrial production grew 6.7%, compared with 4.2% a year ago.Manufacturing , which has a weight of 76% in the index, grew 9% as 18 out of 23 industry groups witnessed an increase in output, led by motor vehicles, transport equipment, electricals, machinery equipment, computers, rubber and plastics.Electricity and gas supply expanded 12.3% on account of higher temperature due to heat wave conditions. Electricity production from both conventional and renewable sources recorded double-digit growth in Aug. The newly added water supply, sewerage and waste management sector grew 6.3%. Activity in the mining and quarrying contracted -5.6% during the month.In the use-based category -- capital goods (16.9%), intermediate goods (13.7%) and infra goods (12%) industries registered double-digit output, reflecting the impact of sustained public capex in the economy. Consumer durables, too, recorded 11.1% growth during the month.Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said revival in industrial growth is a positive sign as this has been witnessed in the last few months. "Growth in credit to industry has also been very high and broad-based, supporting the hypothesis of the sector recovering quite rapidly this year to contribute positively to overall growth," he added. ICRA Ratings chief economist Rahul Agrawal said IIP growth in July-Aug has averaged 7.7%, up from 6.2% in April-June quarter, which should partly offset the likely impact of margin pressure stemming from the renewed surge in global commodity prices, on the July-Sept growth.You use AI every day. articles.title: UAE may invest another $25bn: Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Union minister of commerce Piyush Goyal said UAE investors have expressed intent to invest another $25 billion, on the back of $25 billion already
articles.body: MUMBAI: Union minister of commerce Piyush Goyal said UAE investors have expressed intent to invest another $25 billion, on the back of $25 billion already invested, with an eventual objective of taking investments in India to $100 billion.Citing the Emirates NBD investment in RBL and IHC's acquisition of a stake in Sammaan Capital, Goyal said UAE has invested $25 billion in India and is the seventh-largest source of foreign direct investment."We are also exploring the possibility of UAE becoming a more important source of LPG and other energy supplies that we require. A study is also underway to see whether we can develop subsea pipelines through which gas can be transported and stored in India, strengthening our energy resilience and security," said Goyal. The two sides also discussed expanding cooperation in shipbuilding, modern ports, space technology, agri-innovation, logistics, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, energy security and fintech.India and UAE are also discussing increasing the use of the rupee and dirham for bilateral trade. Goyal said local currency trade is currently in double digits and is expected to continue growing."If we have to pay for imports in dirham and receive rupee payments for exports, we can periodically convert the balances into dollars," said Goyal, addressing a press meet on Monday. Bankers said that since the UAE dirham is pegged to the dollar at a fixed rate, bilateral trade in local currencies is viable, liquid and low risk.The comments came after India and UAE held the 14th meeting of the High-Level Joint Task Force on Investments, where the two sides discussed investments, trade facilitation, taxation, logistics, energy, market access and financial cooperation.Goyal said the task force had become an effective mechanism to resolve challenges faced by investors and address issues related to the implementation of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).The CEPA is now four years old and bilateral trade has doubled to $100 billion, Goyal pointed out.You use AI every day. articles.title: OpenAI shelves new AI model after internal safety tests, WSJ reports
articles.summary: Sept 28 () - OpenAI is scrapping the release of GPT-6.1 Astra, a next-generation AI model planned ‌for an October debut, over safety concerns raised ‌by rese...
articles.body:
Sept 28 (Reuters) - OpenAI is scrapping the release of GPT-6.1 Astra, a next-generation AI model planned ‌for an October debut, over safety concerns raised ‌by researchers during internal testing, the Wall Street Journal reported on ​Monday.

The model, expected to appear in ChatGPT and Codex, was designed to handle more complex tasks without human assistance, the report said.

Earlier this month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called ‌for the industry ⁠to slow the development of frontier AI models to allow safety measures to keep pace, ⁠a view endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

OpenAI did not immediately respond to a ​Reuters ​request for comment.

The ChatGPT parent's ​safety chief Saachi Jain ‌told the Journal on Monday that Astra fell short of the company's standards in alignment tests, which assess whether a system follows human intent.

The model showed more deception than its predecessor, including at times failing to accurately ‌disclose actions it had or ​had not taken, the report said.

It ​also had problems ​with "scope authorization", pushing ahead with tasks without ‌requesting user permission and sometimes ​attempting to use ​external tools or services when doing so could be unsafe.

The decision comes ahead of OpenAI's developer ​conference in San ‌Francisco, where the company has previously unveiled products ​aimed at software developers.

(Reporting by Akash Sriram in ​Bengaluru; Editing by Vijay Kishore)

articles.title: AMD just spent $8.2 billion to enlist the 'Godmother of AI'
articles.summary: In spending $8.2 billion to scoop up World Labs, AMD CEO Lisa Su has gained the "Godmother of AI" and possible successor for when the time comes.
articles.body:
In spending $8.2 billion to scoop up World Labs, AMD ( AMD ) CEO Lisa Su has gained an AI innovator and possible successor for when the time comes.

AMD announced late this afternoon an agreement to acquire World Labs , an AI model lab based in San Francisco that focuses on software for 3D environments.

The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.

World Labs was founded in 2024 and is led by Dr. Fei-Fei Li, a leading AI researcher known in tech circles as the "Godmother of AI." She was once the chief scientist at Google ( GOOG ) Cloud.

Li will join AMD as an executive vice president and chief scientist. The direct reporting line to Su underscores the pivotal role Li will play in shaping AMD amid the unprecedented AI boom.

At the same time, Li will add new operational layers to her resume by working closely with one of the most well-regarded CEOs in tech , including a greater presence on Wall Street and executing big deals like the one Su struck with Meta ( META ) this year.

AMD shares rose slightly in after-hours trading.

"This is a talent and model-insight buy, not a revenue play. AMD gets the people building the models its future chips will have to run. Fei-Fei made the case from her side: 'Without having a focused hardware effort, AI is hobbled in efficiency,'" tech analyst Patrick Moorhead said.

Citigroup analyst Atif Malik also shared an initial reaction to AMD's latest bout of dealmaking.

"By adding Dr. Fei-Fei Li and her team, AMD gains deeper visibility into how AI models are evolving, which strengthens its competitive position against NVIDIA and accelerates its broader AI platform ambitions," Malik wrote. "We believe the motivations for this transaction include: 1) acquiring more leading AI engineers; 2) better position the company within physical AI, and 3) build better end-to-end systems. We maintain AMD as our favorite growth compute semis pick in 2026."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. articles.title: Nearly half of Peak XV’s new Surge cohort are AI-native companies
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Peak XV Partners’ seed-stage investing platform Surge is backing 18 early-stage startups building across AI, robotics, space, consumer,
articles.body: MUMBAI: Peak XV Partners’ seed-stage investing platform Surge is backing 18 early-stage startups building across AI, robotics, space, consumer, healthcare, music and fintech as part of its latest cohort. The set of fledgling startups reflects three shifts playing out across early-stage technology: familiar consumer behaviours being rebuilt around new expectations; AI moving from a feature to the underlying architecture of products; and technology increasingly leaving the screen to tackle physical infrastructure and the real world.In an interaction, Rajan Anandan, MD, Peak XV and Surge said that about 50% of them are essentially AI native companies that are either reimagining consumer experiences or providing the infrastructure required to safely deploy AI across the enterprise. “But what's also interesting is, you know, we have a bunch of companies that go beyond AI, right? So, we have our first medical products company. They're actually in stealth. We have an education company, it's actually an offline education company. They're currently in stealth. We also have a space tech company,” Anandan said.It is premature to say that India has lost the AI race, Rajan said. “We couldn't be more excited about AI in India. Right. I think a lot of the public narrative is rightly focused on the capital markets, public AI stocks. But if you look at the private markets, at the application layer, you're looking at hundreds of companies,” Rajan said, adding that there are a lot of opportunities in voice and consumer AI spaces here.“Voice AI will be the first billion dollar revenue category in India. And when it comes to consumer AI, India has more consumer AI startups than the US,” Rajan said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India's Essar Group to invest $18 billion in 'largest' US steel plant, Trump announces
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday announced plans by Indian conglomerate Essar Group, through its US subsidiary Mesabi Metallics, to invest about $18
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Monday announced plans by Indian conglomerate Essar Group, through its US subsidiary Mesabi Metallics, to invest about $18 billion in a major steel plant in Iowa.Trump made the announcement at the White House alongside Essar Group co-founder Ravi Ruia and Mesabi Metallics chairman Rewant Ruia, describing the project as the largest steel plant in American history."Today we're thrilled to announce that Mesabi Metallics will be building the largest steel plant in American history in the great state of Iowa. It's the largest plant, one of the largest plants in the world, but it's the largest plant in America by far," Trump told reporters.The facility is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of steel a year once fully operational, with production targeted to begin in 2030. The project is also expected to create thousands of jobs during construction and nearly 2,000 permanent positions across the steel and mining operations.Project to link Minnesota iron ore mine with Iowa steel plantThe Iowa plant will form part of an integrated US supply chain, with iron ore sourced from a new mine being developed by Mesabi Metallics in Minnesota's Mesabi Iron Range. The company has invested about $2.5 billion in the mine, which is expected to produce around 7.5 million tonnes of iron annually and create about 350 jobs.Rewant Ruia said he was born in India but had studied in New York, Boston and California, adding that he had spent half his life in the US and described the investment as "a true homecoming". He said the project would establish a fully integrated supply chain "from mine to mill".Trump highlighted the domestic nature of the operation, saying the Minnesota mine would be "the first new iron ore mine in the United States in more than 50 years with the highest quality ore.""In other words, this steel will be mined, melted, and made right here in the USA, which is something very unusual," Trump said.Rewant Ruia thanked the president "for bringing back the importance of building things in America." He also said the plant would use advanced technology and "will compete head-to-head with any steel plant in the world on size, quality and on cost."Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick attributed the investment partly to the administration's steel tariffs. Trump said companies were building in the US "because they don't want to pay tariffs".You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
